mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within the last month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are revised downwards.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in slowdown periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 1% within the last two months signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic growth prospects improve.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) increase by more than 5% and real GDP (GDPC1) increases by more than 0.5% within the last quarter, it signals a strengthening demand environment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer confidence and economic activity rise.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increase > 5% and GDPC1 increase > 0.5% in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2% within the last month, it signals a strengthening labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment increase.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 200,000 and UNRATE decrease > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 2% signals inflationary pressures, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as real returns are eroded and the Fed may tighten monetary policy.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in inflationary periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year change in real GDP (GDPC1) is positive and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) remains stable (less than 2% increase), it signals a healthy demand environment without significant inflationary pressures, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY increase > 0% and CPIAUCSL YoY increase < 2%
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
